newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW - UK December PPI data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - UK December PPI data.

text.p: Following is a selection of economists' reactions to UK December producer price data showing input prices down s/a 0.5 pct m/m and down 5.9 percent y/y, while output prices rose 0.5 percent m/m amd 1.7 percent y/y.
The Reuters consensus forecast was for input prices to fall 0.9 percent m/m and 6.6 percent y/y and output prices to rise 0.8 percent and 2.0 percent respectively.
"I think one should concentrate on the core (output price) figure of 0.8 percent. This continues the excellent performance of last month. That is the major message from the data."

"If the Chancellor wants to keep interest rates steady at Wednesday's monetary meeting, this morning's PPIs give him useful ammunition with which to argue his case. Key number is the core factory gate price index. This was up just 0.1 percent, leaving the annual rate at less than one percent and so well below the key RPIX...The headline output price index will have been boosted by budget effects so a worryingly large looking 0.5% gain...can be ignored. Prospect for subdued inflation outlook helped by another fall in manufacturers' raw material and fuel costs."

"Data support the view that competitiveness factors are still holding down prices at the factory level, even if the pickup in consumer spending has allowed for some modest widening of selected margins at the retail level. Positive for short sterling and gilts."

"The 0.1 percent monthly increase in core output prices shows nothing much frightening coming through the pipeline... We're seeing very good news in input prices and even in output prices, yet retail price inflation at the back end of last year was moving higher...Clarke probably has the option after today's numbers and last week's of delaying a rate rise a little. It's still very difficult to see how he can avoid a rate rise this side of the election."
